description: A set is composed of the printings that belong to it; a printing belongs to exactly one set and loses its release context without it.

connection_condition: cards.scryfallOracleId identifies the card identity that all its printings share
description: A card identity is composed of its printings across sets and years; each printing is one concrete realization of the identity.

connection_condition: faces share the printing uuid and are distinguished by cards.side and linked by cards.otherFaceIds
description: A multi-face printing is composed of its faces; a face has no independent printing record.
A reprint is a specific kind of printing, namely one that is not the first appearance of its card identity; reprint rows are a subset of all printing rows.
Converted mana cost is derived from mana cost by summing the amount of mana the symbols represent.
Rulings are attached to a printing; a ruling row has no meaning detached from the card printing it clarifies.

connection_condition: indirect: a card identity is reached from rulings only by grouping all printings that share scryfallOracleId, and identical ruling text repeats across those printings
description: Rulings describe how a card works, so they are conceptually about the card identity, but they are stored per printing and must be deduplicated before being attributed to a card.

connection_condition: indirect: localized rows are keyed by printing uuid, so a card identity must be reassembled from its printings and repeated translations deduplicated
description: Localized card text belongs to a card identity but is stored once per printing per language.

connection_condition: no structural link: legalities stores no set reference, so the format card pool can only be related to sets through set release dates
description: A format's card pool follows which sets are within its window, which is why the same cards differ in legality across formats.

connection_condition: each legalities row pairs one format value with one status value
description: Every format assigns a legality status to the printings it covers; absence of a row is itself meaningful because no explicit not-legal value exists.
Translated set names are components of the set record; a translation cannot exist without its set.
A release date is a defining property of a set rather than an independent entity; it orders sets in time and bounds format card pools.

connection_condition: both are comma-separated color lists on the same printing row and coincide for most printings
description: Card color and color identity are closely related but not equivalent: color identity also includes colors of mana symbols that appear in rules text, so the two differ for cards with off-color abilities.
